entries.description: AnyPS5 – это набор утилит, позволяющих автоматически преобразовать исполняемые файлы PlayStation 5 в нативные форматы Linux и Windows. Основу составляет «relinker», который переписывает бинарник под целевую ОС и подключает реализованные системные PRX‑библиотеки, избавляя от эмуляции и отдельного рантайма. Инструмент работает на macOS (включая Apple silicon) и предоставляет веб‑конвертер, где файлы остаются на устройстве пользователя. Поддерживается ввод через SDL‑совместимые контроллеры, клавиатуру и мышь, а также генерация SPIR‑V шейдеров при включённом модуле Spirv‑Tools. Проект ориентирован на исследователей, архивистов и разработчиков, желающих запускать PS5‑игры на ПК без нарушения авторских прав, и распространяется под GPL‑2.0.

# About

Tool for automatic executables porting to Linux and Windows.

The relinker-only build runs on macOS, including Apple silicon.

[**Web converter**](https://boykopovar.github.io/AnyPS5/) - files stay on your device.

![anyps5_collage1](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ed2f0b2d-33d3-46d7-ab88-767ca872fc99)

Includes a [relinker](core/relinker) that converts executable to the target system's native format and implementations of [system prx libraries](core/libs/prx) suitable for dynamic linking. No emulation or separate runtime process.

[**Discord**](https://discord.gg/BHFztBPUe), [Usage](docs/user/USAGE.md), [Build instructions](docs/dev/BUILD.md), [Architecture](docs/dev/ARCHITECTURE.md), [Technical debt of the project](docs/dev/TechnicalDebt.md), [code style conventions](docs/dev/CONVENTIONS.md), [contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md)

## Status

[![libraries](https://boykopovar.github.io/AnyPS5/badge-libraries.svg)](https://boykopovar.github.io/AnyPS5/progress.html) [![shaders](https://boykopovar.github.io/AnyPS5/badge-shaders.svg)](https://boykopovar.github.io/AnyPS5/progress.html)

[![progress map](https://boykopovar.github.io/AnyPS5/progress.svg)](https://boykopovar.github.io/AnyPS5/progress.html)

[Progress history](https://boykopovar.github.io/AnyPS5/history.html)

<sub>* System libraries: percentage of the functions known to the project so far (declared in [core/libs/prx](core/libs/prx)), not of every PS5 system function. The total grows as more functions are declared.</sub>

Unsupported or unexpected states strictly throw `std::runtime_error`. `what()` is printed to stderr and the process terminates.

The [shader recompiler](core/shader/recompiler/Recompiler.cpp) successfully produces SPIR-V (validated via [Spirv-Tools](3rdparty/SPIRV-Tools) when built with `ANYPS5_ENABLE_SPIRV_TOOLS`).

## Compatibility

Per-game progress (stage reached, open blockers, libraries and GPU coverage) is tracked on the [blocker map](https://alxcbtw.github.io/anyps5-roadmap/), a community project built from public GitHub data ([source](https://github.com/AlxcBTW/anyps5-roadmap)). Test reports go in the [Game bring-up](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/discussions/categories/game-bring-up) discussions, one thread per title.

## Input mapping

SDL-mapped game controllers are supported, including analog sticks and triggers. Keyboard and mouse controls can be configured with an `anyps5-input.ini` file. See [input mapping](docs/user/INPUT_MAPPING.md) for the supported devices and configuration format.

## Disclaimer

This project is intended for interoperability, research, preservation, and compatibility purposes. It does not include, distribute, or require copyrighted software, firmware, cryptographic keys, or proprietary libraries. Users are responsible for ensuring that any binaries used with this project are obtained and used in accordance with applicable laws and their respective license terms.

latest.readme_excerpt: # Ghidra Software Reverse Engineering Framework Ghidra is a software reverse engineering (SRE) framework created and maintained by the [National Security Agency][nsa] Research Directorate. This framework includes a suite of full-featured, high-end software analysis tools that enable users to analyze compiled code on a variety of platforms including Windows, macOS, and Linux. Capabilities include disassembly, assembly, decompilation, graphing, and scripting, along with hundreds of other features. Ghidra supports a wide variety of processor instruction sets and executable formats and can be run in both user-interactive and automated modes. Users may also develop their own Ghidra extension components and/or scripts using Java or Python. In support of NSA's Cybersecurity mission, Ghidra was built to solve scaling and teaming problems on complex SRE efforts, and to provide a customizable and extensible SRE research platform. NSA has applied Ghidra SRE capabilities to a variety of problems that involve analyzing malicious code and generating deep insights for SRE analysts who seek a better understanding of potential vulnerabilities in networks and systems. # Claude Code Plugins Directory

A curated directory of high-quality plugins for Claude Code.

> **⚠️ Important:** Make sure you trust a plugin before installing, updating, or using it. Anthropic does not control what MCP servers, files, or other software are included in plugins and cannot verify that they will work as intended or that they won't change. See each plugin's homepage for more information.

## Structure

- **`/plugins`** - Internal plugins developed and maintained by Anthropic
- **`/external_plugins`** - Third-party plugins from partners and the community

## Installation

Plugins can be installed directly from this marketplace via Claude Code's plugin system.

To install, run `/plugin install {plugin-name}@claude-plugins-official`

or browse for the plugin in `/plugin > Discover`

## Contributing

### Internal Plugins

Internal plugins are developed by Anthropic team members. See `/plugins/example-plugin` for a reference implementation.

### External Plugins

Third-party partners can submit plugins for inclusion in the marketplace. External plugins must meet quality and security standards for approval. To submit a new plugin, use the [plugin directory submission form](https://clau.de/plugin-directory-submission).

## Plugin Structure

Each plugin follows a standard structure:

```
plugin-name/
├── .claude-plugin/
│   └── plugin.json      # Plugin metadata (required)
├── .mcp.json            # MCP server configuration (optional)
├── commands/            # Slash commands (optional)
├── agents/              # Agent definitions (optional)
├── skills/              # Skill definitions (optional)
└── README.md            # Documentation
```

## Plugin names are immutable

The `name` field in a marketplace entry is an **immutable slug**. Once a plugin has been published, its `name` must not change — users have it installed under that slug, and renaming it breaks their install with a `plugin-not-found` error.

- To change how a plugin is labeled in the UI, set or update `displayName` instead.
- If a rename is genuinely unavoidable, add an entry to the top-level `renames` map in `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` so existing installs auto-migrate:

```json
"renames": {
  "old-name": "new-name"
}
```

The Claude Code plugin loader reads this map and transparently rewrites the old slug to the new one on the user's next sync.

## Skill-bundle plugins

When a plugin's source repository ships skills (`SKILL.md` files) without a `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` manifest, the marketplace entry can declare the skills directly using `strict: false` and an explicit `skills` array.

```json
{
  "name": "example-bundle",
  "description": "Brief description of the bundled skills.",
  "author": { "name": "Author Name" },
  "category": "development",
  "source": {
    "source": "git-subdir",
    "url": "https://github.com/example-org/sdk.git",
    "path": "packages/agent-skills",
    "ref": "main",
    "sha": "<commit sha>"
  },
  "strict": false,
  "skills": [
    "./skill-a",
    "./skill-b",
    "./skill-c"
  ],
  "homepage": "https://github.com/example-org/sdk"
}
```

Each path in `skills` is relative to `source.path` and points at a directory containing a `SKILL.md`. Paths can reach deeper than a single level — for example, `["./libA/skill-1", "./libB/skill-2"]` exposes a curated subset across multiple library subdirectories. Each skill is registered as `<plugin-name>:<skill-name>` in Claude Code.

For the underlying schema, see [Strict mode](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces) in the marketplace documentation.

## License

Please see each linked plugin for the relevant LICENSE file.

## Documentation

For more information on developing Claude Code plugins, see the [official documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins).

Quit Claude Code mid-task, > start OpenAI Codex in the same directory, continue without > re-explaining the architecture, the failed approaches, or the open > questions. **Website: [aimemory.sh](https://aimemory.sh)** [![Website](https://img.shields.io/badge/website-aimemory.sh-blue)](https://aimemory.sh) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/akitaonrails/ai-memory)](https://github.com/akitaonrails/ai-memory/releases/latest) [![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/rust-1.95+-blue)](rust-toolchain.toml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE) ## Why ai-memory Your coding agent probably has a memory feature already. Claude Code takes its own notes, Cursor remembers some things, and every platform is adding more. They all have the same limits: the notes live on one machine, belong to one agent, and drop out of view when you switch tools or hand the work to a teammate. ai-memory removes those limits. - **It follows you across agents.** More than twenty harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Grok, Devin, Kimi, Kiro, and others) feed one shared memory. Quit Claude Code mid-task, open Codex in the same directory, and the next agent picks up a handoff that says where you left off, what failed, and what is still open. Handoffs are a typed protocol: each one has an owner and is claimed exactly once. - **It can carry the session, not just a summary.** Start agents with `ai-memory run`: quit Claude Code, run `ai-memory run codex`, and Codex gets the shared workstream plus a private, temporary local projection of Claude's visible native history for exact details the bounded startup packet omitted. The remote server receives only the harness and session identity, never the local transcript path or body. Direct harness launches behave exactly as before. - **It follows you across projects.** A small profile of how you usually work (your package manager, test layout, architecture habits) reaches every new repository at session start, so you stop re-explaining yourself. It sits below each repository's rules file as a default. It is on by default for a single user, and on a shared server it is opt-in and private per person. See [`docs/cross-project-profile.md`](docs/cross-project-profile.md). - **It follows you across machines.** Memory lives in a server you run, on the same laptop, a homelab box, or anywhere else, so the project you left on the desktop is the project you resume on the laptop, with the same knowledge and the same open questions. - **It works for a team.** Point everyone at one server, and what one person's sessions learn, everyone's agents can retrieve. Knowledge is shared per project; personal handoffs stay personal. Multi-user auth, per-person attribution, and an audit log are built in and are not a paid tier. - **Your memory is plain markdown.** The source of truth is a git-backed wiki of ordinary `.md` files: `grep` it, open it in Obsidian, edit it by hand, `rsync` it. The database is a derived index that can always be rebuilt from the files. There is no vector store to maintain and no content locked in a binary blob. - **It captures the work itself, silently.** Lifecycle hooks record what happened (prompts, tool calls, session boundaries), sanitize it at a typed privacy boundary before anything is stored, and the server consolidates it into readable pages. You do not have to ask it to remember anything. The default path uses **zero LLM calls**: capture, search, and handoffs all work with no API key. - **It ages memory without an LLM.** Memory decays on a schedule you can tune per tier, and memory you use decays *slower*: opening a page, searching it, or reaching it through a link counts as use. When episodic notes go cold they can be compacted down to their durable facts (file paths, error codes, decisions) instead of dropped. Near-duplicates collapse into one, and likely contradictions get flagged, all with **zero API calls**. Nothing is hard-deleted: the original stays in git and the version chain (`restore-page` brings it back). Access-weighted retention is always on because it can only keep memory *longer*. The parts that rewrite or drop content (compaction, dedup, per-tier curves) stay off by default until you turn them on. - **It can also "dream", if you let it.** With an LLM configured, an opt-in background pass rewrites whole clusters of cold notes into single coherent pages while you are idle, and cancels as soon as you come back to work. # Marble Skill Taxonomy

An open, structured taxonomy of **what children learn** across the primary/elementary years — decomposed into fine-grained "micro-topics", wired into a prerequisite graph, and aligned to national curriculum standards. Produced by [Marble](https://withmarble.com).

> **Version:** `v1` · **Topics:** 1,591 · **Prerequisite edges:** 3,225 · **Subjects:** 8

## See it

![The taxonomy as a rotating 3D graph: every dot a micro-topic, colored by subject, wired by prerequisites](media/curriculum-viz.gif)

Every dot is a micro-topic, colored by subject; height is age; each thread is a prerequisite ([full-quality video](media/curriculum-viz.mp4)). Explore it interactively at [withmarble.com/curriculum](https://withmarble.com/curriculum) — tap any concept to trace everything a learner must master before it.


## What this is

Most curriculum data is either a flat list of standards or locked inside a product. This dataset is a **connected graph of learning**:

- **1,591 micro-topics** — a single, teachable idea (e.g. *"Building sentences"*, *"Apparent brightness of stars"*), each with a plain-language description, mastery **evidence** criteria, a type (conceptual / procedural / representational / language / meta), a subject + domain, and an approximate age range.
- **3,225 prerequisite dependencies** — a directed acyclic graph: *"topic X depends on prerequisite Y"*, each edge tagged `hard`/`soft` and carrying a one-line **reason**.
- **Curriculum alignment** — each micro-topic links to the standards it was distilled from (NGSS, Common Core, the UK National Curriculum, and more).
- **Teaching research** — 1,051 records covering the current Science and Mathematics topics: teaching approaches, concrete learning activities, feedback, assessment guidance and linked sources. Coverage is partial; the other 540 topics have no research in this release.
- **Domain clusters** — 176 parent-friendly one-paragraph summaries per (subject, domain, age band).

### Subjects

| Subject | Topics |
|---|---:|
| Science | 547 |
| Mathematics | 504 |
| English | 286 |
| History | 90 |
| Personal & Social Development | 88 |
| Life Skills | 37 |
| Computing | 21 |
| Learning to Learn | 18 |

## Files

All data lives in [`data/`](data/) as UTF-8 JSON. See [`schema/`](schema/) for JSON Schemas and [`manifest.json`](data/manifest.json) for counts + SHA-256 checksums.

| File | What it holds |
|---|---|
| [`data/topics.json`](data/topics.json) | The micro-topics (graph **nodes**). |
| [`data/dependencies.json`](data/dependencies.json) | Prerequisite **edges** (`topicId` depends on `prerequisiteId`). |
| [`data/curriculum-standards.json`](data/curriculum-standards.json) | The source curriculum standards, grouped by curriculum. |
| [`data/clusters.json`](data/clusters.json) | Parent-friendly domain summaries. |
| [`data/teaching-research.json`](data/teaching-research.json) | Teaching research joined by `topicId`, with explicit coverage and publication notes (~24 MB). |
| [`data/manifest.json`](data/manifest.json) | Counts, per-subject breakdown, per-file checksums. |

### A topic

```json
{
  "id": "mt_N8CpN1EJrP",
  "type": "CONCEPTUAL",
  "subject": "English",
  "domain": "Grammar & Punctuation",
  "name": "Building sentences",
  "description": "Understand that words combine to make sentences — a sentence expresses a complete thought…",
  "ageRangeStart": 4,
  "ageRangeEnd": 6,
  "centrality": 0.257,
  "evidence": [
    "Distinguish between complete sentences and fragments",
    "Compose a complete sentence with a subject and verb"
  ],
  "assessmentPrompt": "If {{name}} says something like \"The dog\", can they tell you that's not a complete sentence…?",
  "standards": ["ccss-ela:L.K.1f", "uk-nc-2013:Eng.App2.Y1.Sent.1"]
}
```

- `id` — stable identifier (`mt_…`), referenced by dependencies and by neighbours.
- `standards` — keys into `curriculum-standards.json` (`"<curriculum-slug>:<code>"`).
- `assessmentPrompt` — a natural-language check for the idea. Contains a `{{name}}` placeholder (the child's name); substitute or strip before display.

### A dependency

```json
{ "topicId": "mt__00ZSLnB7p", "prerequisiteId": "mt_VBl1T1sFCM", "strength": "hard",
  "reason": "Must understand vibrations make sound before finding volume patterns" }
```

`topicId` **depends on** `prerequisiteId`. Reverse the edge to get "unlocks".

## Teaching research

[`data/teaching-research.json`](data/teaching-research.json) adds **how a topic
might be taught** to the graph of what children learn. It covers **547 Science**
and **504 Mathematics** topics. `coverage.missingTopicIds` and per-subject counts
make the **540 topics without research** explicit; absence is not a judgement
about whether a topic can be taught.

The file has `schemaVersion: 1` and taxonomy `version: "v1"`. Each `records[]`
entry joins `topics.json` through `topicId` and contains:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `pedagogy` | Original teaching summary, practices, representation

# earshot

**Ears for coding agents.**

<!-- launch video -->
[**Watch the 22 s launch film**](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/earshot/releases/tag/v0.1.0) - every sound in it was made
in code by `earshot forge`; no recordings, no music track.

![Frames from the launch film](docs/media/launch_frames.png)

AI coding agents can now write the code that renders a film, a product demo or a game. They still cannot hear what
they made. They cannot tell a premium key press from a cheap one, notice that a hit lands 80 ms after the cut, or
hear that the music swells in the wrong place.

earshot turns sound into evidence an agent can reason about: what a file sounds like in words, how well it fits a
description, the best moment inside a long recording, whether it is a real recording or code-synthesized, a
second-by-second listening transcript of a whole film, an annotated picture of it, and a scorecard against
professional launch films. It runs locally on CPU, as a CLI, a Python API and an MCP server.

With ears, an agent can also **make its own sounds in code** and improve them by listening (`earshot forge`), and
**translate a recording into code** it can vary (`earshot fit`). Both below.

**New in 0.3: sound for code-made films.** A bank of 201 sound effects stored as code that render by id in seconds,
with no models and no network: `earshot sfx` aims a whoosh, hit, click or note at a moment in the picture, and
`earshot kit` renders a whole film's effects with measured sync points ([below](#sound-for-films-bank-sfx-kits)).

```
$ earshot describe enter.ogg
  0.56 s short transient (attack 3 ms, decays in 190 ms). Sounds most like: a single mechanical keyboard key press
  (z +5.4), a soft key release click (z +3.6) ... [clear reading]. peak -0.1 dBFS, brightness 1.5 kHz ...

$ earshot match key.ogg "a deep thocky mechanical keyboard press" --alts "a clicky blue switch keyboard" "a mouse click"
  -> strong (z +3.7; would rank #2 among 322 vocabulary descriptions) ...

$ earshot find keys.ogg "a single mechanical key press" --top 4
  0:03.94-0:04.19 (0.24 s stroke, z +4.1 strong); 0:10.60-0:10.86 ...

$ earshot critique film.mp4
  VERDICT: close - 21 of 23 scored metrics in range ... FIX FIRST: 1. [major] nothing reaches body level until 0:01.01 ...
```

## What it does

| command | what an agent gets |
|---|---|
| `describe FILE` | what it sounds like: calibrated tags (z) with the closest alternative readings, AudioSet labels, measurements |
| `match FILE QUERY [--alts ...]` | how well a description fits: cosine, z among the vocabulary, a verdict (strong / plausible / weak / no match) with held-out evidence |
| `rank QUERY PATHS...` | many candidate files sorted by a description (pick the best download) |
| `find FILE QUERY` | the best moments inside a long recording, as sample trims (start / end seconds) |
| `compare FILE --refs DIR` / `ab A B` | nearest reference recordings and typicality; A/B two sounds or two trims, the differences in words |
| `realness FILE...` | real recording / pro-produced vs code-synthesized, with evidence and per-window scores |
| `timeline FILE [--video V] [--cues C]` | the listening transcript: events (time, level, tag), sections, loudness, beat grid, sync of sound to picture cuts and cue frames |
| `sheet FILE -o out.png` | an annotated PNG (video frames, sections, labelled events, spectrogram, waveform, loudness, sync markers) for agents that read images |
| `critique FILE [--video V]` | a launch-video scorecard against a profile of 7 professional launch films, with timestamped fixes |
| `profile REFS... -o p.json` | build your own reference profile from films you admire |
| `measure FILE` | objective measurements only (no models): LUFS, true peak, LRA, envelope, spectrum, tempo / key |
| `forge RECIPE --refset CAT` | make a sound in code and improve it by listening (see below) |
| `fit FILE -o recipe.py` | translate a recording into a forge recipe module that re-renders it, with knobs and morphs (see below) |
| `sfx render ID -o x.wav` | a sound from the shipped bank of 201, aimed at the picture (`--dur`, `--apex`, `--pitch`) and audited; `sfx list`, `sfx check` (no models) |
| `kit init / render / check` | a film's sound kit: one bank sound per role, rendered into cached takes with measured onset / peak / end (no models) |
| `gallery DIR -o page.html` | one static HTML listening page of forge outputs: players, spectrograms, numbers |
| `llm FILE --yes-upload` | optional audio-LLM critique (Gemini), only with your own key and explicit consent |
| `mcp` | the same tools as an MCP server for Claude Code and other agents |
| `doctor [--load]` | check the install, models, data files and CPU settings |

Every command prints a plain-language summary first; `--json` gives the full result, `--out f.json` saves it. Errors
are one line on stderr (`earshot <command>: error: ...`, exit 1). Each CLI call is a new process and loads the models

## Português

Port nativo do **Shadow of the Colossus** de PS4 (Bluepoint, 2018; CUSA08809, versão EU 1.01)
para **Windows 10/11**. O código x86-64 do próprio jogo roda direto na CPU do PC e a GPU do PS4
é traduzida para Vulkan. Não é um emulador completo: é um carregador com as funções de sistema
de que o jogo precisa, no estilo do [bloodborne_pc](https://github.com/Supermedo/bloodborne_pc).

### Novidades

| Versão | Melhorias e correções |
|---|---|
| **0.57** | **Placas AMD:** correção das cores verdes/rosas na névoa e nos personagens (as AMD passam a usar o caminho de 32 threads da NVIDIA; diagnóstico da issue #7, ainda não testado numa AMD). **Opção nova** no lançador para desligar o acesso direto à memória: ~10% mais FPS, água distante mais lisa. |
| **0.56** | **Água do mundo aberto com ondas:** lagos e rios abaixo das cascatas não ficam mais lisos como espelho (uma instrução de shader, `S_WQM_B64`, era ignorada). **Lago de cima ondula e reflete até longe** (acesso direto à memória ligado por padrão, como no Pink-shadPS4). Árvores distantes sem "lixo colorido". |
| **0.0.13** | **Sem quedas:** corrigida a queda na abertura/menu da 0.0.12 (o jogo pedia mais texturas do que cabe no pool). Testado ~40 min pelo mapa, com dois carregamentos de save. **Reflexos do lago** em quase toda a superfície, com ondulação (uma trava de laços dos shaders cortava os raios do reflexo). |
| **0.0.12** | **Texturas nítidas de volta, sem o jogo fechar:** a corrupção de memória que derrubava o jogo depois de carregar um save foi corrigida, e o streaming de texturas voltou (pedras e paredes bem mais nítidas). **Água:** respingos, anéis e espuma ao nadar; o lago reflete o céu e o brilho do sol; reflexos de ambiente com o *cubemap* certo de cada *probe* (correção do Pink-shadPS4). |
| **0.0.11** | Corrigida a grama com textura de "lixo colorido" da 0.0.10. |

Detalhes de cada versão no [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md).

### Problemas conhecidos

- Na primeira abertura depois de atualizar, os shaders são compilados de novo: o primeiro
  carregamento demora e engasga.
- Placas **AMD**: a 0.57 traz a correção das cores verdes/rosas ([#7](../../issues/7)), ainda sem
  teste numa AMD. Se continuar, mande o seu `user/last_run.log` na issue.
- Com 8 GB de memória de vídeo, o uso fica perto do limite em áreas grandes.

1. Baixe o `SotC-PC.zip` da página [Releases](../../releases) e descompacte numa pasta.
2. Abra o **`SotC.exe`**. Na primeira vez o lançador procura sozinho, nos discos do PC:

# mcp-for-blender-pro

### Your Blender scene. Your AI models. One creative workspace.

**An AI assistant for Blender that can inspect your scene, build objects, edit materials, find assets and carry out multi-step workflows—with a visual chat workspace and a built-in Model Context Protocol (MCP) server.**

![Blender 4.2+](https://img.shields.io/badge/Blender-4.2%2B-E87D0D?logo=blender&logoColor=white)
![Release 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/release-1.0.0-98D85B)
![Windows x64](https://img.shields.io/badge/download-Windows_x64-357EC7)
![MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)

[Download](../../releases/latest) · [Getting started](docs/QUICKSTART.md) · [Connections and agents](docs/CONNECTIONS.md)

![AI chat workspace with a live Blender scene preview](docs/images/studio.png)

## Turn a creative brief into scene operations

Start with an idea. Ask the assistant to inspect your scene, create a product-display layout, arrange objects, assign materials or prepare an export. Follow its actions in the conversation and inspect the result in the viewport preview. Keep working in Blender throughout the process.

**mcp-for-blender-pro brings conversation, scene tools, model choice and agent workflows together.** It is designed for artists who want faster iteration, technical artists who automate repetitive work, and developers connecting AI tools to Blender.

## Why choose mcp-for-blender-pro?

| Capability | What it gives you |
|---|---|
| **Blender-aware assistance** | Scene and object inspection gives the assistant context before it acts. |
| **A visual Studio workspace** | Chat, scene objects, viewport snapshots, approvals and a task board in a companion window. |
| **Your choice of AI** | Connect supported cloud providers, local Ollama models or compatible custom endpoints. |
| **Saved connections** | Keep work and personal connections separate, including multiple keys for the same provider. |
| **One assistant or a team** | Use a single model for quick changes, or managers, workers and reviewers for structured tasks. |
| **Built-in MCP server** | Connect OpenCode and other clients supporting authenticated Streamable HTTP MCP. |
| **21 scene tools** | Create, inspect, edit, capture, search assets, consult Blender APIs and export scenes. |
| **Multilingual menus** | Choose English, German, French, Spanish or Chinese for the main interface. |

## From a quick edit to an agent team

Use **Single assistant** for direct, conversational work. For larger tasks, configure a **Team chain** with individual responsibilities, instructions and models.

- **Manager:** breaks the request into assignments and acceptance criteria.
- **Workers:** perform the assigned scene operations.
- **Reviewers:** inspect results and approve work or return specific findings.

Tasks run sequentially so scene edits stay ordered. A blocked task gets one correction attempt; a second failed review stops the workflow. The task board exposes assignments, attempts and review findings as work progresses.

![Agent roles and model configuration](docs/images/studio-team.png)

## Connect the models that fit your work

Supported connections include **OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, OpenRouter, OpenCode Zen, Ollama and custom APIs**. Load the available model catalog and select a model directly in Blender or Studio.

Custom endpoints support OpenAI Chat Completions, Anthropic Messages and Ollama protocols. Choose models with tool-calling support; image-capable models can also interpret viewport screenshots. OpenCode-only free models are available through the OpenCode client.

![Provider, saved connection and model selection](docs/images/studio-settings.png)

## Install and create

1. Download **`mcp-for-blender-pro.zip`** from [Releases](../../releases/latest).
2. In Blender, open **Edit → Preferences → Get Extensions → menu → Install from Disk**.
3. Select the ZIP, enable **mcp-for-blender-pro**, then open **3D Viewport → N → MCP Pro**.
4. Choose a provider, add your connection details and select a model.
5. Send a message in Blender or click **Open Studio Window**.

The release bundle targets **Windows x64 with Blender 4.2 or later**. Keep Blender open while using Studio or an external client.

English · Русский

Your PS5 game store.
Back from the dead, rebuilt from its own binary, with every line of source in the open.

Install · Features · Updates · Troubleshooting · Build it yourself

> [!NOTE] > The original Overdrive project has been shut down so I decompiled the last released build, > recovered the complete source and rebuilt it.

## Features - **1,800+ games** to discover, with **Top rated**, **New releases** and a featured spotlight - **Browse the whole library** with filters, sorting, scores and download sizes at a glance - **Downloads straight to the console**, to internal storage or any USB drive, with live speed and storage stats - **Favorites**, **search** with an on-screen keyboard, and a **Files** page to see and clean up what's on your drives - **16 languages**: English, Deutsch, Español, Français, Italiano, Nederlands, Português (Brasil), Русский, Bahasa Indonesia, 日本語, 简体中文, العربية, فارسی, اردو, हिन्दी, বাংলা - **Updates itself**: a new version installs from the console, no PC needed - Made for the controller: L1 R1 to switch sections, ✕ to select, ○ to go back ## Install in four steps

### Before you start You need a **jailbroken PS5** running two payloads: **[ShadowMount+](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus)**, which installs `.exfat` images by itself, and **[kstuff](https://github.com/EchoStretch/kstuff-lite/releases)**. If ShadowMount+ shows its notification when the console starts, you are ready. You also need a **USB drive** and a **PC**.

**Download `Overdrive.exfat`** with the button above, or from the [latest release](https://github.com/MyLuxy/overdrive/releases/latest). It is the only file you need. Leave it as it is: don't unzip it and don't change the `.exfat` at the end of its name.
**Copy it onto a USB drive, inside a folder called `homebrew`.** Plug the drive into your PC, create a new folder named exactly `homebrew` (all lowercase) at the top level of the drive, and copy `Overdrive.exfat` into it: ```text USB drive └── homebrew └── Overdrive.exfat ``` The drive must be formatted as **exFAT**, which is how most drives come and what the PS5 reads.
**Plug the drive into the PS5.** ShadowMount+ checks for new files every few seconds: it finds Overdrive, mounts it and installs it, and a notification tells you when it's done. There is nothing to click.

latest.readme_excerpt:
# GPTibo

**可自托管的数字商品商城，包含用户前台、管理后台与代理工作台。**

[![CI](https://github.com/CoolkHz/gptibo/actions/workflows/verify.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/CoolkHz/gptibo/actions/workflows/verify.yml)
[MIT License](LICENSE) · [快速开始](#快速开始) · [后端文档](services/storefront/README.md) · [安全说明](SECURITY.md)

GPTibo 将商品展示、下单支付、订单交付、售后处理和代理商店管理整合在同一套系统中。前端使用 React 与 TypeScript，后端提供 Go + PostgreSQL 和 Cloudflare Workers + D1 两种实现，便于按部署环境选择和二次开发。

原站点已停止运营，项目现以 MIT 许可证开放源码。支付与供应商接入使用匿名适配器，需要配置自己的服务后使用。

## 功能

| 模块 | 能力 |
| --- | --- |
| 用户商城 | 商品与套餐展示、下单、支付状态、订单查询、售后申请、中英文界面、深浅色主题 |
| 管理后台 | 商品定价、订单与客户管理、退款处理、代理管理、结算与通知配置 |
| 代理工作台 | 独立商店、品牌设置、自定义域名、商品管理、订单统计与下级代理管理 |
| 业务后端 | 身份验证、支付回调、采购适配、异步任务、邮件通知与交易状态管理 |
| 开发与部署 | 数据库迁移、Docker Compose、自动化测试、GitHub Actions 与源码安全扫描 |

## 技术栈

| 层级 | 技术 |
| --- | --- |
| 前端 | React 19、TypeScript、Vite、Tailwind CSS |
| Go 后端 | Go、Gin、PostgreSQL，API 与业务 Worker 分进程运行 |
| Cloudflare 后端 | Workers、D1、Wrangler |
| 邮件 | React Email |
| 验证 | Node.js Test Runner、Go Test、Gitleaks |

两套后端均服务于商城。当前公开版本包含商城侧供应商适配器，**不包含独立供货平台及供应商执行系统**。

## 快速开始

### 环境准备

- Node.js 24、npm、Git、Python 3。
- 使用 Go 后端时，准备 Docker Compose；原生开发需要 Go 1.26+ 和 PostgreSQL。
- 使用 Cloudflare 后端时，通过项目内的 Wrangler 运行本地环境。

```sh
git clone https://github.com/CoolkHz/gptibo.git
cd gptibo
npm ci
```

选择下面一种后端方式运行。

### 方式一：Go + PostgreSQL

在仓库根目录执行以下命令，初始化本地秘密、数据库和运行角色：

```sh
cd services/storefront
python3 scripts/init-secrets.py
cp .env.example .env
docker compose config --quiet
docker compose build api
docker compose up -d --wait postgres
docker compose --profile maintenance run --rm maintenance migrate
docker compose --profile maintenance run --rm maintenance grant-runtime
docker compose up -d --wait api worker
```

另开终端，在仓库根目录启动前端：

```sh
npx vite --config services/storefront/vite.config.ts
```

访问 `http://127.0.0.1:5175`。前端会将 `/api` 请求代理到本机 Go API 的 `8093` 端口。

原生启动、管理员登录、邮件服务与接入配置见 [Go 后端文档](services/storefront/README.md)。Windows 用户可使用后端目录中的 `scripts/init-secrets.ps1` 初始化秘密。

### 方式二：Cloudflare Workers + D1

在仓库根目录执行：

```sh
cp .dev.vars.example .dev.vars
npx wrangler d1 migrations apply gptibo-local --local
npm run preview:worker
```

默认访问 `http://127.0.0.1:8787`。需要前端热更新时，另开终端运行 `npm run dev`，访问 `http://127.0.0.1:5173`；API 请求会转发到本地 Worker。

`.dev.vars` 保存本地配置，不应提交。远程部署时需创建自己的 Cloudflare 资源，并替换 `wrangler.jsonc` 中的占位配置。

### 页面入口

| 页面 | 路径 |
| --- | --- |
| 商城 | `/` |
| 管理后台 | `/admin` |
| 代理工作台 | `/partner` |

管理员登录需要配置自己的管理员身份、TOTP 和邮件验证服务。默认配置不提供可直接登录的管理员账号，也不会发起真实支付、采购或通知。

## 项目结构

```text
src/                   商城前台、管理后台与代理工作台
services/storefront/   Go API、业务 Worker、迁移与部署配置
worker/                Cloudflare Workers 后端
migrations/            D1 数据库迁移
emails/                邮件模板
tests/                 前端与 Worker 业务测试
scripts/               构建与源码检查脚本
public/                静态资源
.github/workflows/     持续集成
```

## 配置与接入

| 配置文件 | 用途 |
| --- | --- |
| [services/storefront/.env.example](services/storefront/.env.example) | Go 后端基础运行配置 |
| [services/storefront/.env.integrations.example](services/storefront/.env.integrations.example) | Go 后端支付、采购及通知接入 |
| [.dev.vars.example](.dev.vars.example) | Cloudflare 本地配置 |
| [wrangler.jsonc](wrangler.jsonc) | Worker 与 D1 资源配置 |

供应商适配器使用 `recharge`、`account_supplier`、`delivery_supplier`、`xgift` 等通用名称；`gatewaya`、`gatewayb` 为匿名聚合支付适配器。请依据自己的服务协议核对地址、签名、商品映射、金额和回调，再开启对应功能。

真实商户身份、密钥、账号凭据和生产数据不随源码提供。`example.invalid` 是不可用于真实接入的保留域名，示例商品与金额仅用于演示。请使用新数据库安装；匿名化后的迁移不兼容原生产数据库。

## 开发与验证

在仓库根目录执行：

```sh
npm test                # 前端与 Worker 业务测试
npm run lint            # 静态检查
npm run build           # 类型检查、邮件模板与前端构建
npm run security:scan   # 公开源码检查
```

Go 后端验证：

```sh
cd services/storefront
go test ./...
go vet ./...
```

完整数据库测试需设置 `STOREFRONT_TEST_DATABASE_URL`，连接本机、库名以 `_test` 结尾的专用数据库；未配置时集成测试会跳过。详细要求见[后端测试说明](services/storefront/README.md#测试)。

自动化测试不连接真实支付或供应商服务。生产部署前，需要在自己的环境验证完整交易流程。

## 参与贡献

欢迎通过 [Issues](https://github.com/CoolkHz/gptibo/issues) 反馈问题或提出建议，也欢迎提交 Pull Request。

1. 描述问题、预期行为和复现步骤。
2. 提交范围明确的改动，涉及交易或账务逻辑时补充回归测试。
3. 运行与改动相关的检查，在 PR 中说明验证结果。

请勿提交真实凭据、用户资料、生产日志或数据库。安全问题请按 [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) 中的方式报告。

## 许可证

项目代码采用 [MIT License](LICENSE)，允许在保留版权与许可声明的前提下使用、修改和分发。

第三方资源遵循各自许可证，商标及美术作品权利归原权利人所有。详见[品牌资源说明](public/brands/README.md)与[第三方样式说明](src/styles/vendor/README.md)。

# imozuru 日本語 | [English](README.en.md) imozuruは、知らない分野を、原文にたどりつくまで芋づる式に掘るClaude Codeのスキルです。 Batesのberrypicking、Ellisの探索行動のモデル、Kuhlthauの探索過程の研究など、図書館情報学の情報探索の研究から、考え方を応用しています。 ## ふつうに頼んだときとの違い スキルなしで「調べて」と頼むと、LLMは検索上位の数件を読んで要約を返します。 要約はすぐに読めますが、判断に必要な細部が落ちやすい欠点を抱えています。 分野の用語を知らないうちは検索語も選べないため、最初に思いついた言葉の範囲から先へ進めません。 imozuruはまず分野の用語、中心にいる人、知見が集まる場を押さえ、そこから引用やリンク、著者をたどって原文を集めます。 集めた原文は要約せずに保存し、答えに必要な主張ごとに「どのファイルの何行目か」を示すに留まります。 原文を読んで判断するのは、ユーザー自身です。 ## 動き方 ```mermaid flowchart LR A[問いと
要る主張を書く] --> B[地図づくり
用語・人・場] B --> C[たどる
引用・リンク・著者] C --> D[原文を落とす] D --> E{要る主張に
原文が付いた？} E -- まだ --> C E -- 付いた・飽和した --> F[抜き書きの
ページを作る] ``` Claudeはまず、問いと、答えるために必要な主張を3〜6個書き出します。 次に、探し方を変えた2本の検索役（Webを検索するサブエージェント）で用語、人、場を集め、地図（`map.md`）にまとめます。 その後、原文が見つかるまで参考文献や被引用、著者をたどっていきます。 論文のない分野では、記事の中のリンクや「〇〇さんの記事を参考にした」という記述をたどります。 見つけた原文は `sources/` に保存し、404やログインを求めるページは中身を見て除きます。 すべての主張に原文が付くか、新しい資料が出てこなくなったら探すのをやめます。 最後に、原文から切り出した文を主張ごとに並べたページ（抜き書きのページ）を作ります。 見張りのモードでは、掘って見つけた場（QiitaやZennのタグ、note、YouTube、ブログ、arXiv）の新着をRSSで集めて並べます。 ## 入れ方 [skills](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) のCLIで入れられます。 ```sh npx skills add MaryCache/imozuru ``` 手動の場合は、`skills/imozuru/` を `~/.claude/skills/imozuru/` にコピーしてください。 ## 必要なもの スクリプトはPython 3.10以上の標準ライブラリだけで動き、次のコマンドは入っていれば使います。 | コマンド | 使う場面 | 入っていない場合 | |---|---|---| | `pdftotext`（popplerかXpdf） | PDFから本文を取り出す | PDFの本文が取れず `FAIL` になる | | `pdftoppm`（popplerかXpdf）と `tesseract` | 文字の層がない古いPDFをOCRにかける | そのPDFは `FAIL` になる | | `yt-dlp` | YouTubeの字幕を取得する | 動画は `FAIL` になる | | [ax](https://github.com/yusukebe/ax) | HTMLをmarkdownにする | 標準ライブラリで文字だけを取り出す（見出しや表の形はaxのほうがよく残る） | 引用をたどる `chain.py` は [OpenAlex](https://openalex.org/) のAPIを使いますが、APIキーは必要ありません。 ## 使い方 Claude Codeで、次のように頼みます。 ``` 芋づる式に調べて: 歌ってみたのMIXで、上手い人がどういう順番で処理しているか ``` ``` Gaussian Splattingってよく聞くけど全然わからない。論文とか解説の流れを掘ってほしい ``` ``` /imozuru watch react ``` 結果は `~/research/<話題>/` に、次の形で保存されます。 ``` map.md 問い・要る主張・用語・人・場・原文の表・次の手がかり log.md 周ごとに、何を探して何が出たか・判断とその理由 sources/ 落とした原文 extracts.json 抜き書き report.html 抜き書きのページ ``` 抜き書きのページの見本は `examples/demo/` にあり、次のコマンドでスクリプトだけを試せます。 ```sh python3 skills/imozuru/scripts/report.py examples/demo ``` ## 設計の考え方 ### 要約しない理由 Kuhlthau（1991）は、調べ始めの混乱した段階で詳しくまとめると、早すぎる閉じ（premature closure）を招き、探索の過程が妨げられると述べています。 そのためimozuruは、原文の場所を示すところまでにとどめています。 ### 止めどきの決め方 止める条件は2つです。 1つ目は、すべての主張に原文の場所が付くことで、証拠がそろったかで止めどきを決めるRohとHan（2026）のHALTにならいました。 主張が甘くならないよう、少なくとも1つは依頼の言葉の条件をそのまま含め、半分以上は原文を読まないと答えられない形にしています。 2つ目は飽和で、2本の検索役が挙げた資料の7割以上がすでに地図にあれば止めます。 独立した2回の探索の重なりから全体の数を見積もる考え方（Kastner 2007）を借りたもので、7割は試しながら決めた仮の目安です。 ### 方向を1つに決めない理由 Zhouら（2026）のHypoSearchによると、AIの検索は方向がいくつもありうる段階で1つを選び、後の検索でもその道を選び続けて失敗しがちです。 そこで迷ったときは、別の仮説を持たせた検索役を2本並べ、結果を比べてから進みます。 ### 論文のない分野の扱い 塗り方やMIXのように論文がほとんどない分野では、知見の多くが個人のブログや動画にあります。 imozuruはそうした記事も論文と同じようにたどるので、保存した原文には次の印を付け、どれを信じるかはユーザーに任せています。 - 〔論文〕査読や学会を通ったもの、arXivのプレプリント - 〔本人〕やった本人の記録（自分で試した、作った、測った過程が書いてあるもの） - 〔観察〕他人の作品ややり方を見て、特徴を書き出したもの - 〔まとめ〕他人の知見を集めたり言い換えたりした記事 - 〔公式〕道具や製品を作った側の文書 ### 抜き書きを機械で照合する理由 原文を何十本も保存しただけでは、どこから読めばよいか分かりません。 そこでEllisのモデルにある抜き書き（extracting）にならい、主張ごとに原文の該当部分を切り出したページを作ります。 `report.py` は、切り出した文が原文の指定の行にそのまま在るかを照合し、1語でも違えばページを作りません。 ## 決まりの出典 スキルの各決まりがどの論文のどこから来ているかは、`skills/imozuru/references/theory.md` にまとめています。 ## 注意点 - 検索役はWebを検索するため、問いの内容が検索語として外部に送られます。機密情報や個人データが関わる調べものには使わないでください。 - 有料の論文を回避して入手する手段は使わず、取得できなかったものは「届かなかった」と報告します。 - 保存した原文は手元で読むための写しなので、再配布しないでください。 ## # web-ocean

A real-time ocean renderer written from scratch on WebGPU, with no engine or rendering library. It draws a sunset sea with simulated waves, whitecaps, sun glitter, and a physically based sky with clouds. You fly around it with a free camera.

![Looking toward the sun from 2.4 m above the water](docs/front.jpg)

| 75 degrees off the sun, 2.4 m up | Looking toward the sun from 30 m up |
|---|---|
| ![](docs/side.jpg) | ![](docs/high.jpg) |

## Run it

You need a recent Chrome with WebGPU and a reasonably capable GPU. On a laptop, force Chrome onto the dedicated GPU in the Windows graphics settings, or it will fall back to the integrated one.

Open `ocean.html` directly in the browser. `ocean.min.html` is the same page minified (61 KB instead of 102 KB). Both are self-contained and work from `file://`.

To run from source:

```
npm install
npm start        # serves http://localhost:8080/
```

After editing anything under `js/`, run `npm run build` to regenerate both bundles. The minified build strips WGSL comments and whitespace and minifies the JavaScript with esbuild.

## Controls

| Input | Action |
|---|---|
| Click the canvas | Capture the mouse (Esc releases it). Holding the right mouse button also works. |
| Mouse | Look around |
| W A S D | Move |
| Space or E / Q or C | Up / down |
| Shift | 5x speed |
| Mouse wheel | Change base speed |
| H | Settings panel: wind, swell, choppiness, turbidity, foam, sun, haze, clouds, exposure, bloom |

The camera keeps itself above the displaced water surface, so waves never pass through it.

URL parameters are handy for testing. `?w=2560&h=1440` forces the render resolution, `cam=x,y,z,yawDeg,pitchDeg` sets the camera, `fov=deg` sets the field of view, `ui=0` hides the HUD, and any settings key works too, for example `windSpeed=12&swellHs=2&sunElev=8`.

## How it works

### Waves

The sea is a Tessendorf FFT simulation with six cascades of 256 by 256 samples. The patches range from 1103 m down to 0.26 m, so wavelengths run from about a kilometre to a few millimetres. The smallest cascade produces the sharp sun sparkles near the camera.

The spectrum is a fetch-limited JONSWAP wind sea with Donelan-Banner directional spreading, plus a narrow long-crested swell. Dispersion includes the capillary term, and choppy horizontal displacement sharpens the crests. The inverse FFTs are radix-2 compute shaders working in workgroup memory.

The surface mesh is a CDLOD quadtree with 17 levels. Vertices are 6.25 cm apart near the camera and the mesh reaches 160 km, with continuous vertex morphing between levels.

### Shading

- Mip-mapped first and second moments of the wave slopes (LEAN mapping) give the right anisotropic roughness at every distance. The sun glitter widens with distance and the far sea settles into a sheen without aliasing. Screen-space slope derivatives add specular anti-aliasing.
- Sun glitter uses an anisotropic Gaussian slope distribution with Smith masking and the size of the solar disc.
- The sky reflection comes from an environment cube map rebuilt every frame, with roughness-filtered mips. At grazing angles the reflection direction is tilted to account for which wave facets the viewer can actually see.
- The water body is turbid blue-green, lit by the whole sky hemisphere. Backlit crests get a subsurface glow, and wind-gust patches modulate the short ripples.
- Whitecaps start where the total surface Jacobian folds. Foam is stored in two camera-centred world-space maps (128 m and 1 km wide), decays over time, drifts downwind, and breaks into streaks as it ages. A procedural bubble texture gives it its structure.

### Sky

The atmosphere follows Hillaire's approach, with transmittance, multiple-scattering, and sky-view lookup tables plus aerosol haze. There are two cloud layers, a broken low cumulus and a fibrous altostratus deck. Each is shaded with self-shadowing toward the sun, lit rims, silver linings when backlit, and direction-dependent multiple scattering.

Cloud noise octaves are filtered by pixel footprint, and silhouettes are anti-aliased analytically: the screen-space derivative of each layer's edge function sets the width of its opacity edge. Cloud transmittance along the sun direction dims the sunlight that reaches the water, and aerial perspective is applied over the sea.

### Post-processing

The scene renders in HDR with 4x MSAA. Post-processing adds an 8-level bloom, AgX tone mapping, a slight white balance shift, and dithering.

## Performance

At 2560 by 1440 on an RTX 5070 Ti, the GPU takes about 6 to 8 ms per frame, measured while other programs were also using the GPU. The HUD shows FPS and GPU time when the browser supports `timestamp-query`.

The per-frame code reuses preallocated typed arrays and descriptors, so the garbage collector has almost nothing to do. The only recurring allocations are the objects WebGPU itself requires, such as the swap-chain view and command buffers.

overview: На этой неделе в открытом сообществе доминировали инструменты, упрощающие работу с AI‑агентами и их интеграцию в различные среды: REA расширяет возможности обратного анализа, а Headroom снижает токенные расходы за счёт компрессии контекста. Практические задачи автоматизации кода и данных решаются проектами OpenCode, Claude Code и Ruflo, которые позволяют генерировать, планировать и координировать действия агентов прямо в терминале или через плагины. Для творческих специалистов вышли ArtCraft и ComfyUI, предоставляющие визуальные среды для генерации изображений, видео и 3‑D‑контента без написания кода. Наконец, проекты вроде AnyPS5, ShadowOfTheColossus‑PC и Overdrive показывают, как открытый софт может переносить закрытые платформы и игры на новые операционные системы, а Kronos открывает возможности предсказаний на финансовых данных. Все эти решения будут полезны разработчикам, исследователям и креативным профессионалам, ищущим гибкие и открытые альтернативы коммерческим продуктам.
